title: Area of Circle: Archimedes Exhaustion Method

problemStatement.formal: exhaustion_equals_ftc (r : ℝ) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => inscribedArea n r) Filter.atTop (nhds (∫ ρ in (0 : ℝ)..r, circumference ρ))
problemStatement.plain: Can Archimedes' classical exhaustion method be formally connected to the modern FTC-based proof that A = ∫₀ʳ C(ρ) dρ? Both methods compute πr² via different limiting processes; by Hausdorff uniqueness they must agree.
whyMatters: Connects two millennia of mathematical development: Archimedes (250 BCE) and Newton/Leibniz (17th century)
Formalizes the implicit Hausdorff assumption in Archimedes' double exhaustion argument
Proves sin(h)/h → 1 rigorously from the derivative definition, completing the Archimedes → FTC bridge

proven: exhaustion_equals_ftc: both methods converge to the same value
inscribed_area_le_pi_r_sq: inscribed areas ≤ πr² (via sin(x) < x)
